eyebrow: The T-SQL Development Course · Chapter Nine
subtitle: Lesson 110 · Transactions, Locking, and Isolation Levels

eyebrow: The real view behind everything in this chapter
code:
SELECT resource_type, resource_database_id,
       request_mode, request_status,
       request_session_id
FROM sys.dm_tran_locks;
caption: Every lock currently granted or waiting, system-wide, right now.

eyebrow: The four columns that matter most
code:
-- resource_type:     OBJECT, PAGE, KEY, RID
-- request_mode:      S, X, U, IS, IX, SIX, Sch-S, Sch-M
-- request_status:    GRANT (held) or WAIT (blocked)
-- request_session_id: the SPID holding/waiting for it
caption: Matches exactly the lock types covered across this chapter.

eyebrow: Session A holds, Session B waits
code:
-- Session A: UPDATE ... WHERE ProductID = 680; (open)
-- Session B: SELECT ... WHERE ProductID = 680; (blocks)

SELECT resource_type, request_mode, request_status,
       request_session_id
FROM sys.dm_tran_locks
WHERE request_session_id IN (@spidA, @spidB);
caption: A's row: KEY/X, GRANT. B's row: KEY/S, WAIT.

code:
-- Something "just hanging" in production?
-- Check sys.dm_tran_locks FIRST, before guessing.
